name: Muka
method: Equal-weighted, 35 holdings, paper index only (no real money). Return is the average of the holdings' daily returns, so it behaves as if rebalanced daily. Prices adjusted for dividends. European companies are held as US-listed shares (ADRs), so every return is in US dollars and no currency conversion is needed.
rules: The board meets monthly, on the 2nd of the month (Melbourne time).
At most 3 swaps per meeting, and no more than 8 holdings in any one theme.
A holding can be dropped when its trend has failed (below its 50-day and 200-day averages) at two month-end checks in a row, or when its theme story breaks.
A replacement comes from the bench and must be in an uptrend at the meeting. Each swap is written to the log with a reason.
Recent insider buying (officers and directors buying with their own money) can break a tie between replacement candidates, but is never a reason on its own.
Every change takes effect from the latest US close before the meeting and is never back-dated.

board.text: Founding portfolio: 35 holdings across 8 themes, amended before the first trading day to add a Europe theme (ASML moved from AI Compute). Growth engines (AI compute, platforms, power) are balanced by defensives, healthcare, financials, hard assets and European leaders so one bad theme cannot sink the index.
